hero_kpi_rationale_en: Robust growth of 24% to $5.2 Bn in 2025, reflecting the acceleration of global solar energy deployment and strong demand for U.S.-manufactured photovoltaic modules

ai_positioning.summary_en: First Solar recognizes the growing demand for energy capacity driven by AI-powered data centers, which are increasing overall electric load and utility-scale solar energy demand, but is not developing any AI-specific products or services.
evidence_en: utility and corporate demand for energy and overall electric load growth, especially as a result of AI-driven data center demand, continue to increase

risks.title: Regulatory Risk
risks.score_rationale_en: The company is highly dependent on advanced manufacturing tax credits under the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA). Legislative or regulatory changes could materially reduce these financial benefits

risks.title: Pricing Competition Risk
risks.score_rationale_en: The solar industry is characterized by intense pricing competition, with numerous Chinese competitors having access to sovereign capital or forms of government support, which could compress margins

risks.title: Foreign Currency Exchange Risk
risks.score_rationale_en: The company's subsidiaries in multiple countries have cash flows denominated in currencies other than their functional currency, exposing the company to foreign exchange risks

risks.title: Supply Chain Risk
risks.score_rationale_en: The company has a global manufacturing footprint spanning the U.S., India, Malaysia, and Vietnam, making it vulnerable to supply chain disruptions and trade tariffs

risks.title: Customer Concentration Risk
risks.score_rationale_en: In 2025, the company terminated supply agreements with BP Solar and Lightsource, resulting in $384.6 M in termination payments and a legal action for recovery

risks.title: Manufacturing Capacity Expansion Risk
risks.score_rationale_en: The company is building its sixth manufacturing plant in the U.S., scheduled to begin operations in the second half of 2026, which carries risks of delays and cost overruns
